mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which typically precedes earnings downgrades and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 3%, signals aggressive tightening and heightened inflation risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.75% AND CPIAUCSL monthly change > 3%
regime_hint: high inflation and rapid rate hikes
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) increase of less than 50,000 while the unemployment rate is below 4% indicates labor market softening despite low unemployment, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: labor market softening under low unemployment
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 2% for four consecutive months signals persistent weakness in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of the business cycle phase.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 2% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals broad-based contraction in supply and demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.
